Topic 3.4: Creative writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Creative writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when writing creative texts texts), in pairs and groups paragraphs?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines)

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Creative writing helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines)

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines). You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines).
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Creative writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines). Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Creative writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Creative writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines))

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Creative writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines).
3. Make one local Kenya example of Creative writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Creative writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Creative writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when writing creative texts texts), in pairs and groups paragraphs?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Creative writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate a sense of ownership in writing competitions at school and 184 the written work through various media (newspaper, children magazines).

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
